notes: The VWAP reclaim signal genuinely beats random entries (+0.046R, t=3.06 on discovery) but loses money because a 1-minute stop is so tight that fixed costs of 0.06-0.08R swamp it; running the identical logic on 5-minute bars makes each trade's risk roughly three times larger, so the same signal keeps its edge while costs shrink to a small fraction of R. name: Recovery swing triggered on the daily EMA, not the intraday EMA
notes: The setup is defined by price losing the prior day's daily EMA, so the meaningful confirmation is price closing back above that same daily level; reclaiming a 15-minute EMA is a much weaker, noisier event, and switching the trigger level should give fewer but cleaner trades with a bigger margin over random entries. Builds on re-d5194badb1 (NBIS recovery swing v0.1, failed screen): The trigger level only: reclaim_level goes from the chart EMA to the daily EMA. Arming, breakout confirmation, stop and exits are unchanged, and it is run on the whole universe rather than on NBIS alone as in the earlier hand test.

name: Daily-EMA recovery swing, no trigger on the session's first bar
notes: When the first 15-minute bar of the session closes back above the prior day's daily EMA, the 'reclaim' is usually an overnight gap through the level rather than buyers winning it back during the day, so it carries none of the setup's information and a stop under that bar's lows is hit by ordinary opening noise. Taking the same daily-EMA reclaim only once the session has traded should keep the real reclaims and drop the gap-throughs. The trader's own journal points the same way independently: their entries from 09:30 to 09:45 lost money while 09:45 to 10:00 was their best window. Builds on re-d5bbe25d57: The entry window only: fills allowed from 10:00 instead of any time, which removes triggers on the first 15-minute bar (09:30-09:45) of each session. Trigger level (daily EMA), arming, breakout confirmation, stop, 2R target and two-session hold are unchanged. Drawn from the discovery evidence, so the screen is not an independent test of it.

name: Daily-EMA recovery swing with a one-hour stall exit
notes: The recovery swing bets that a reclaim of the prior day's daily EMA holds. A real reclaim should show itself quickly: buyers who won the level back keep price above the entry. A trade that is still at or below its entry an hour (four 15-minute bars) after the trigger is a reclaim that did not hold, and most of those go on to the full -1.1R stop instead of the 2R target. Leaving such trades at the one-hour mark, usually for a fraction of R, should cut the average loss on failed reclaims while every trade that is working runs on to the unchanged 2R target or two-session exit, where this pattern earns its money. The trader's own journal of about 1,573 real trades points the same way independently: their winners were usually closed within an hour, and trades still open after an hour and closed the same day lost money in every period checked. Random entries get the same stall rule, so this passes only if the signal's trades separate from random ones within that first hour. Builds on re-a9765cdc93: The exit only: add a stall exit at 60 minutes with stall_r 0, so a trade leaves at the close of the bar that brings the hold to one hour unless that close is above the entry. Trigger level (daily EMA), the 10:00 start of the entry window, arming, breakout confirmation, stop, 2R target and two-session hold are unchanged.

name: Opening range breakout, skipping breaks on the first bar after the range
notes: With a 5-minute opening range, a close beyond it on the very next 5-minute bar (09:35-09:40) is still part of the opening auction's noise: the range is one bar wide, so the stop is tight and the first swing back through it takes the trade out. A break that comes once the open has settled (from 09:45) is more likely to be real directional flow, and holding it to the close lets it run. On the discovery period the default family's breaks signalled at 09:40 averaged about -0.64R over roughly 1,430 trades while breaks from 09:45 on were positive, and the trader's own journal of about 1,515 option trades independently found entries from 09:30 to 09:45 lost money, 09:45 to 10:00 was the best window, and entries after a 5-minute opening range break beat their other entries in both years and on both sides. Random entries get the same window, stop rule and hold, so this passes only if later breaks themselves beat random entries. New idea: The entry window only: fills allowed from 09:45 to 16:00 instead of any time, so a break on the first bar after the 5-minute range is refused (and, as the family already does, uses up that side for the day). Range length, both sides, stop at the other side of the range, hold to the close, no target and the session limits stay at the family defaults. Drawn from the discovery evidence, so the screen is not an independent test of it.

name: Opening range breakout on a 15-minute range
notes: A 5-minute opening range is one bar of the noisiest trading of the day, so its high and low are not levels anyone defends and its width gives a stop too tight for the open's swings. A 15-minute range lets the opening auction finish inside the range, so a later close beyond it is a break of a level the market actually built, and the stop at the other side has more room, which also shrinks the fixed costs per R that sank the one-minute patterns. This is the classic longer opening range, a standard coarse value chosen before any result for it was seen, though the idea was prompted by the weak first-bar breaks in the 5-minute family's discovery evidence. New idea: The range length only: range_minutes from 5 to 15 (three 5-minute bars). Timeframe, both sides, stop at the other side of the range, hold to the close, no target, no window and the session limits stay at the family defaults. Drawn from the discovery evidence, so the screen is not an independent test of it.

name: Daily-EMA recovery swing, only when SPY is up on the day
notes: The daily-EMA reclaim is a long-only dip-buy, and it needs the market behind it: on discovery the worst fifth of recovery-swing trades by SPY's intraday move (SPY well below its open) averages about -0.26R while every other fifth is positive, and the one candidate that reached confirmation was strong in the first half and flat in the second, the signature of a strategy that depends on the market's direction. Refusing the setup whenever SPY is below its own session open should drop roughly the worst 40% of trades and lift the per-trade margin over random entries enough to carry the whole period rather than one regime. name: Daily-EMA recovery swing held a third session
notes: The forward evidence for this entry says its edge accrues slowly and keeps growing: against random entries the move after the fill is +0.03R at 30 minutes, +0.05R at an hour, +0.11R at the session close and +0.21R at the next session's close, with no sign of fading. That is a multi-day recovery, not an intraday pop, and the matching failure is the stall exit, which cut trades at one hour and died in confirmation. Exiting at the second session's close therefore closes trades that are still working; giving the same trades a third session should let more of them reach the 2R target and widen the gap over random entries, which are held exactly as long. Builds on re-a9765cdc93 (daily-EMA recovery swing, no trigger on the session's first bar; failed screen at t=1.97): The exit only: max_sessions goes from 2 to 3. Trigger level (daily EMA), the 10:00 start of the window, arming, breakout confirmation, stop and the 2R target are unchanged, and no time or stall stop is added. Drawn from the discovery evidence, so the screen is not an independent test of it.

name: Daily-EMA recovery swing triggered on the reclaim itself, not on a three-bar high
notes: The daily-EMA reclaim is the only entry in the ledger that makes money before costs (+0.15 to +0.19R a trade over random), but at ~400-560 trades it cannot reach the confirmation bar: with about 500 trades in the confirmation window it needs roughly 0.2R a trade over random, and every filter tried so far bought a higher average by throwing trades away. Requiring the reclaim close to also clear the prior three highs does two harmful things: it discards arms where price wins the level back but never clears three bars' highs before the arm expires, and when it does trigger it does so further above the level, which inflates the distance to the stop under the last four lows so the same dollar recovery is worth fewer R. Triggering on the reclaim close that clears only the prior bar's high keeps the identical setup (price traded below the prior day's daily EMA, then closed back above it) while giving more trades and a smaller risk per trade, so the edge per trade should hold or improve and the t should rise through count rather than through a slice of history. Builds on re-a9765cdc93: The trigger's breakout requirement only: breakout_bars from 3 to 1, so the reclaim close need only exceed the prior bar's high. Trigger level (daily EMA), arming, the 0.1-ATR stop under the last four lows, the 2R target, the two-session hold and the 10:00 window start are all unchanged. Note on fitting: the inherited 10:00 window start came from the discovery evidence, but the change being tested here was not read off any result. Drawn from the discovery evidence, so the screen is not an independent test of it.

name: Daily-EMA recovery swing with a three-session arm
notes: The same count problem from the other side: the arm that fires when price trades below the prior day's daily EMA lasts only two sessions, so any dip that needs longer than two sessions to stop falling and win the level back is never traded. Those slower recoveries are the same event the pattern is built on, and the forward evidence says this entry's edge accrues over one to two sessions after the fill rather than in the first minutes, which is the signature of a base that took time to form, not of a fast bounce. Extending the arm to three sessions should add trades of exactly the same kind without changing what is traded or how it is exited, and a quarter more trades at the same per-trade edge is enough to move the screen t from about 1.97 to above 2 and the confirmation t to near the bar. Because the change was not read off any result, a screen pass here would mean the entry itself is better than chance rather than that a slice of history was chosen well. Builds on re-a9765cdc93: One setting only: arm_sessions from 2 to 3, so an arm stays live for three sessions after price trades below the prior day's daily EMA. The trigger (daily-EMA reclaim clearing the prior three highs), the stop, the 2R target, the two-session hold and the 10:00 window start are unchanged. Note on fitting: the inherited 10:00 window start came from the discovery evidence; the change being tested here did not. Drawn from the discovery evidence, so the screen is not an independent test of it.
